Company gains access to more than 53 million U.S. buyers on a platform where beauty is the top category and products listing peptides as an ingredient command the highest average price of any top 10 beauty ingredient

Highlights

  • Approved TikTok Shop storefront: The Company has been approved to operate its own TikTok Shop in the United States, giving it a direct sales channel to more than 53 million U.S. buyers.
  • Approved under tighter rules: The approval follows TikTok's October 2026 move to restrict searches for several peptide names and its stated prohibition on marketing high-risk products.
  • Rollout underway: The first product is live, with further products from the Company's U.S.-made range being brought to the shop, each through TikTok Shop's product review.
  • Peptide products sell at a premium: Beauty products listing peptides as an ingredient generated USD 73.2 million in TikTok Shop sales at a USD 50 average price, the highest of any top 10 beauty ingredient.
  • Verified quality: Every product is made in an approved U.S. facility and backed by a third-party Certificate of Analysis.

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - The Precision Peptide Company (CSE: BPC) (OTCQB: PNGAF) (the "Company"), a publicly traded wellness company focused on advanced peptide formulations and delivery systems, today announced that it has been approved to operate a TikTok Shop storefront in the United States. The first product is now live, with further products from its U.S.-made range to be added as each completes the platform's product review.

The approval comes as TikTok tightens its standards on peptide content, and gives the Company a direct channel to TikTok Shop's 53 million U.S. buyers at a moment when beauty is the platform's largest category, haircare sales have more than doubled, and beauty products listing peptides as an ingredient sell at the highest average price of any leading ingredient.

Approved as TikTok Raises the Bar

In October 2026, TikTok began restricting searches for several peptide names. The platform has said that peptide discussion remains permitted, but that it prohibits the marketing of high-risk products and may restrict searches for unapproved or potentially unsafe products.[10]

The Company's shop was reviewed and approved under those standards. Every product it brings to the platform is manufactured in an approved U.S. facility and supported by a third-party Certificate of Analysis, and as a publicly traded company it reports to shareholders under Canadian securities regulation.

Ingredient-First Products, Rolling Out

With its storefront approved, the Company is bringing its range to the shop product by product, each through TikTok Shop's product review. Every listing names the peptides inside, so shoppers can see exactly what they are buying.

HAIR, the Company's scalp and hair serum, shows the approach. Designed for women who want thicker-looking, fuller-looking hair, it is a simple daily scalp step built around GHK-Cu (Copper Tripeptide-1), the copper peptide that gives the serum its natural blue color. That color is a visible signature of the ingredient, and it comes through on camera, where TikTok Shop products are discovered and sold. HAIR opens the shop in haircare, a category where TikTok Shop sales more than doubled year over year.[7]

Why TikTok Shop

TikTok Shop's U.S. gross merchandise value (GMV) reached USD 15.1 billion in 2025, up 68% from 2024.[1] It then reached USD 11.8 billion in the first half of 2026 alone, up 103% year over year, making the U.S. the platform's largest market.[2] eMarketer forecasts U.S. TikTok Shop sales of USD 23.41 billion for full-year 2026.[3]

The platform had 53.2 million U.S. buyers in 2025,[4] and more of them now arrive with intent: in the first half of 2026, the Shop tab drove 51.4% of U.S. GMV, ahead of video and LIVE.[2] Shoppers who search by ingredient reward brands that can name exactly what is in the bottle, which is how the Company formulates and labels its range.

Beauty & Personal Care is TikTok Shop's largest U.S. category, with an estimated USD 413.1 million in GMV in September 2026, or 17.1% of all U.S. GMV,[5] and USD 1.21 billion across Q3 2026.[6] Haircare alone generated USD 401.1 million in Q2 2026, up 118% year over year.[7] Within beauty, products listing peptides as an ingredient generated USD 73.2 million in sales at a USD 50 average price, the highest of any top 10 ingredient,[9] and four of the top five beauty products in Q2 2026 featured longevity ingredients,[8] a core focus of the Company's peptide formulations.

TikTok Shop extends the Company's direct-to-consumer e-commerce store, its telehealth platform serving all 50 U.S. states, and the nationwide retail sale of its U.S.-made over-the-counter range, which began on July 30, 2026. The launch delivers on distribution expansion, one of the 2027 growth priorities the Company set out in its November 11, 2026 year-end update.

"Winning approval for a TikTok Shop at the same time the platform is tightening its rules on peptides is a real milestone for us," said Pratap Sandhu, CEO of The Precision Peptide Company. "TikTok holds anyone in the peptide space to a high bar, and we built our range to meet it. Every product we bring to the platform is U.S.-made and backed by third-party testing. Our first product is live, and we will keep adding to the shop as each one clears review. This is a bigger step into social commerce for the Company, and we intend to build on it."

Montréal, Québec--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Amex Gold Mining Inc. (TSXV: AMX) (FSE: MX00) (OTCQX: AMXEF) ("Amex" or the "Company") is pleased to announce the achievement of several important underground development and infrastructure milestones at its 100%-owned Perron Gold Project, located near Normétal, Québec, including:

  • 200 metres of underground ramp development completed, marking continued progress toward the fully funded 40,000-tonne bulk sample program.

  • Construction of the 25-kV power line is underway. This power line is designed with capacity to support both the bulk sample program and the future Phase 1 mining operation.

  • Mechanical garage structure has been installed. Majority of the bulk sample site facilities have now been erected and are nearing completion.

Together, these infrastructure improvements contribute to establishing the operational foundation required for the bulk sample and the next stages of underground development and future Phase 1 mining operation at Perron.

Underground Ramp Development Reaches 200 Metres

Underground development at Perron continues to progress, with the main access ramp reaching 200 metres of completed development. To date progress has been steady and on time per construction plans.

Construction of the Power Line Underway

Construction of the approximately 6.5-kilometre, 25-kV power line connecting the Perron Gold Project to the existing electrical grid in Normétal is underway.

The power line is designed to provide approximately 3 MW of electrical capacity, sufficient to support both the ongoing 40,000-tonne bulk sample program and the planned Phase 1 mining operation, as outlined in the Company's Feasibility Study released in April 2026.

This investment represents a step forward in establishing the long-term infrastructure required for Perron. By developing an electrical connection capable of serving both the current bulk sample program and future Phase 1 operations, Amex is strategically positioning the project for its next stage of development while minimizing the need for additional major electrical infrastructure investments.

Once operational, the power line is expected to provide reliable clean hydroelectricity to underground and surface facilities while reducing reliance on diesel-powered generation.

Amex Gold Mining Inc. has made significant high-grade gold discoveries, along with copper-rich volcanogenic massive sulphide (VMS) zones, at its 100%-owned Perron Gold Project. The Perron Project consists of 183 contiguous claims for a surface area of 65.72 km². The project hosts several zones of high-grade gold mineralization, VMS mineralization and 'hybrid' gold-rich VMS mineralization.

When combined with the adjacent and contiguous Perron West Project and Abbotsford and Hepburn Projects (including additional claims acquired through staking) in Ontario, the consolidated land package spans a district-scale 570.94 km². The Project benefits from excellent infrastructure: it is accessible by a year-round road, located just 30 minutes from an airport, and approximately 6.5 km from the Town of Normétal. Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - NexMetals Mining Corp. (TSXV: NEXM) (NASDAQ: NEXM) ("NexMetals" or the "Company") is pleased to report assay results from drill holes SMD-26-217 and SMD-26-216-W1, part of its ongoing surface drilling program at the Selebi Main deposit in Botswana (see Figure 1). The results indicate a newly encountered third mineralized zone below the Lower Zone (the "Third Zone") and extension of the interpreted high-grade trend by approximately 100 metres toward Selebi North, bringing its interpreted length to approximately 1.5 kilometres (the "High-Grade Trend").

SMD-26-217 intersected three distinct mineralized zones. The Main Zone returned 3.15 metres grading 3.14% Cu and 0.86% Ni. The Lower Zone returned 6.60 metres grading 1.35% Cu and 1.95% Ni including 4.25 metres grading 1.33% Cu and 2.37% Ni. The newly encountered Third Zone returned 6.30 metres grading 2.67% Cu and 1.85% Ni, including 4.30 metres grading 2.98% Cu and 2.38% Ni, with higher copper grades than those of the Lower Zone potentially indicating greater remobilization.

SMD-26-216-W1 was an in-fill hole testing a sparsely drilled area approximately 165 metres north of the High-Grade Trend. The hole intersected 1.00 metre grading 2.98% Cu and 1.07% Ni corresponding to the Main Zone and a Lower Zone interval of 3.45 metres grading 2.86% Cu and 1.52% Ni, including 1.45 metres grading 3.61% Cu and 1.94% Ni. SMD-26-216-W1 infills a gap within the resource model on the northern side of the mineralized trend and supports the interpreted consistency of the High-Grade Trend and lateral continuity of the mineralized zones.

Why This Matters

  • New Third Zone expands the exploration opportunity at Selebi Main. NexMetals' first significant intersection below the Lower Zone returned higher copper grades than the Lower Zone in the same hole, alongside strong nickel grades, and indicates increased structural complexity as drilling advances toward Selebi North.

  • The High-Grade Trend has been extended toward Selebi North. SMD-26-217 extendsthe High-Grade Trend to 1.5 kilometres and extended it by approximately 100 metres toward Selebi North while SMD-26-216-W1 supports lateral continuity in the up-dip direction.

  • Lower Zone is demonstrating increasing continuity at depth. Results from SMD-26-213 (7.45 metres grading 2.52% Cu, 1.54% Ni, see news release dated July 22, 2026), SMD-26-219 (7.55 metres grading 2.70% Cu and 1.83% Ni, see news release dated September 23, 2026, together with SMD-26-217 (6.60 metres grading 1.35% Cu and 1.95% Ni, current release) support the interpretation of a laterally and vertically extensive Lower Zone.

  • The system remains open, with further targets to test. Borehole electromagnetic surveying ("BHEM") indicates additional potential mineralization laterally and down plunge. Ongoing drilling and geological modelling are intended to test the extent of all three mineralized zones and target additional areas of thick massive sulphide mineralization.

Sean Whiteford, CEO and Director of the Company, commented: "Our first intersection of the Third Zone returned strong copper and nickel grades below the Lower Zone, providing an additional target for follow-up drilling. Building on the recent 72% increase in Selebi Main's Inferred Mineral Resource to 32.47 million tonnes grading 1.53% copper and 0.97% nickel, these results point to further growth potential as we continue to test the limits of the deposit. SMD-26-217 extends the interpreted High-Grade Trend toward Selebi North, while SMD-26-216-W1 supports potential lateral continuity. We are advancing technical and trade-off studies to support the preliminary economic assessment, while continuing exploration drilling to test the open system."

Qualified Person

All scientific and technical information in this news release has been reviewed and approved by Sharon Taylor, V.P. Geophysics of the Company, MSc, P.Geo, and a "qualified person" for the purposes of National Instrument 43-101 and Subpart 1300 of Regulation S-K.

Quality Control and Data Verification

The program is being executed using three Company-owned underground Zinex U5 drills which were converted into surface A5 drills, and two Marcotte HTM2500 drills purchased by the Company capable of drilling to depths of 2,550 metres (NQ core).

Drill core samples are either NQ (47.75 mm diameter) or BQ (36.40 mm diameter). All samples are ½ core samples cut by a diamond saw on site and the remaining half of the core is retained for reference purposes. Samples are generally 1.0 to 1.5 metre intervals or less at the discretion of the site geologists. Sample preparation and lab analysis were completed at ALS Geochemistry in Johannesburg, South Africa. Commercially prepared blank samples and certified Cu/Ni sulphide analytical control standards with a range of grades are inserted in every batch of 20 samples or a minimum of one set per sample batch. Analyses for Ni, Cu and Co are completed using a peroxide fusion preparation and ICP-AES finish (ME-ICP81). Analyses for Pt, Pd, and Au are by fire assay (30 grams nominal sample weight) with an ICP-AES finish (PGM-ICP23).

Holes are numbered as follows: SMD (Selebi Main Deposit) + year + hole number starting at 201.

The Qualified Person has verified the data disclosed in this news release, including the sampling, analytical and test data underlying the information, through contribution to the core handling and sampling procedures, visits to the drill and core processing facilities, monitoring of core logging results and sample selection, review of core assay and QA/QC results.

For further information regarding the effective date of the 2026 Inferred Mineral Resource Estimate at Selebi Main and the key assumptions, parameters and methods used in its estimation, please refer to the technical report comprising the estimates for the Selebi Main and Selebi North deposits entitled "NI 43-101 Technical Report - October 2026 Mineral Resource Estimate, Selebi Mines Copper-Nickel-Cobalt Project, Botswana", prepared by The MSA Group (Pty) Ltd. with an effective date of October 16, 2026. The technical report has been filed under the Company's profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca, furnished under the Company's profile on EDGAR at www.sec.gov and is also available on the Company's website. The Company has also filed a related Regulation S-K 1300-compliant technical report summary as an exhibit to its Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the period ended September 30, 2026.

BHEM Surveys

The BHEM surveys at Selebi utilize the Crone PEM system operated by local Botswana staff. Survey data is collected using a 3-component fluxgate probe collecting full waveform data. Surveys have been collected using timebases between 50 and 1000ms (0.25 Hz to 5 Hz). The data has been processed to a calculated residual step response to better quantify the conductive sources. This added processing has proven to be highly valuable because of the size of the highly conductive mineralized system.

About NexMetals Mining Corp.

NexMetals Mining Corp. is a TSX.V and NASDAQ listed mineral exploration and development company focused on redeveloping the past-producing Selebi copper-nickel-cobalt mines in Botswana and the Selkirk copper-nickel-cobalt-platinum group element mines in Botswana. NexMetals has confirmed the scale of mineralization is larger than historical estimates, supported by NI 43-101 and Regulation S-K 1300-compliant resource estimates, with ongoing down-hole geophysics, drilling, and metallurgical programs aimed at expanding resources and supporting future economic studies. Cape Town, South Africa--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Lithium Africa Corp. (TSXV: LAF) (FSE: 6MQ) (OTCQB: LTAFF) ("Lithium Africa" or the "Company"), the hard-rock lithium explorer and developer targeting district-scale opportunities across Africa, is pleased to report the discovery of a new lithium-bearing pegmatite system at Jackal Water, 11 km southwest of the Norrabees cluster at its Springbok Project in the Northern Cape of South Africa (the "Springbok Project" or "Springbok"). The first holes intersected stacked pegmatites with up to 56 meters ("m") of logged pegmatite downhole and returned lithium grades of up to 2.21% lithium oxide ("Li2O") over 1.0 m. Together with the Norrabees cluster results reported on November 17, 2026, the Company believes the discovery shows that lithium-bearing pegmatites at Springbok extend well beyond Norrabees, across a district similar in geological style to Brazil's Lithium Valley.

Highlights

  • A new discovery by Lithium Africa's team: Jackal Water was identified using the Company's proprietary, machine-learning-assisted targeting method, developed in-house. The pegmatites are 11 km southwest of the Norrabees cluster and have no known record of previous exploration or drilling (Figure 1).

  • Thick, stacked pegmatites with lithium: all eight reverse circulation ("RC") holes intersected pegmatite, with 11 m to 56 m of logged pegmatite downhole. First assays, received from three of the eight holes, returned 1.0 m intervals of 2.21%, 1.35%, and 0.89% Li2O (Table 1, Appendix). The remaining pegmatite assayed to date returned no significant intercepts, assays are pending from five of the eight holes, and true widths are not yet known.

  • Wide pegmatites along a 50 km trend: spodumene-bearing pegmatites at Springbok are 9 m to 30 m wide in outcrop (not true thickness), along a trend of approximately 50 km on a single 1,675 km² license, and drilling at Jackal Water intersected up to 56 m of logged pegmatite downhole (true width not yet known). For context, Sigma Lithium reports that its Xuxa pegmatite in Brazil's Lithium Valley averages 12 m to 13 m thick; this is not necessarily indicative of mineralization at Springbok.

  • Additional near-surface lithium at Norrabees I: diamond hole NB1DD26-006 returned 9.05 m at 1.19% Li2O from 1.95 m downhole, including 6.0 m at 1.44% Li2O, inside the Company's five-hectare mining permit (Table 1, Appendix).

"Our discovery at Jackal Water takes Springbok from a cluster to a district," said Thomas R. Benson, Ph.D., CEO of Lithium Africa. "Eleven kilometers from Norrabees, our first holes intersected up to 56 m of logged pegmatite downhole and returned up to 2.21% Li2O over 1.0 m. Our project hosts an approximately 50 km trend of lithium-bearing pegmatites similar in thickness to those of Brazil's Lithium Valley, including Sigma Lithium's Xuxa mine (~12-13 m on average), and the results are just starting to come in."

Jackal Water Discovery

The Jackal Water pegmatites (Figure 1) were identified through the Company's in-house targeting method, which combines satellite imagery with machine-learning-assisted analysis of handheld pXRF data, and were confirmed by field mapping. They have no known record of previous exploration or drilling. Eight RC holes (308 m) tested the Jackal Water I and Jackal Water II pegmatites, and all eight intersected pegmatite: 11 m to 24 m downhole at Jackal Water I and 12 m to 56 m downhole at Jackal Water II.

At Jackal Water I, JW1RC26-002 returned 1.0 m at 2.21% Li2O from 10 m and 1.0 m at 0.89% Li2O from 15 m, with elevated cesium ("Cs") and rubidium ("Rb"). At Jackal Water II, JW2RC26-003 intersected 56 m of pegmatite to 57 m downhole and returned 1.0 m at 1.35% Li2O from 45 m, within a 42 m to 47 m zone with elevated Cs and tantalum ("Ta"); the remaining assayed pegmatite returned less than 0.25% Li2O. JW1RC26-003 returned no significant intercept, and assays are pending for the other five holes and for parts of JW1RC26-002 and JW2RC26-003 (Table 1, Appendix).

The Company interprets the enrichment in cesium, tantalum, and rubidium as an indication that highly fractionated pegmatites with the potential to host lithium mineralization occur at both the Norrabees cluster and Jackal Water. This interpretation is preliminary and remains to be tested by further drilling and assays. Intervals and logged pegmatite thicknesses are downhole lengths; true widths are not yet known, and logged pegmatite thickness is not a measure of lithium grade. Collar details are in Table 2 (Appendix).

Three follow-up RC holes (189 m) have since been drilled at Jackal Water, with assays pending, and the Company plans further drilling to test the extent of the pegmatites.



Figure 1: The Springbok Project Prospecting Right (1,675 km²), Northern Cape, South Africa, showing the Jackal Water I and II discovery, the Norrabees cluster and five-hectare mining permit, mapped spodumene occurrences, and key infrastructure. Callouts show selected results from this release and a previously reported result from Norrabees I (see news release dated September 30, 2026). Intervals are downhole lengths, and true widths are not yet known (Table 1, Appendix). Inset shows the Springbok Project location.

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:
https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/11554/324825_d935e21414d28b19_001full.jpg

District-Scale Exploration Potential and Comparison to Brazil's Lithium Valley

Spodumene-bearing pegmatites at Springbok are 9 m to 30 m wide in outcrop, as described in the Company's technical report dated July 21, 2026, along a trend of approximately 50 km on a single 1,675 km² license (Figure 2). Drilling at Jackal Water intersected up to 56 m of logged pegmatite downhole (true widths are not yet known), which the Company believes further supports the potential for thick lithium-bearing pegmatites across the district. For context, Sigma Lithium Corporation's technical report dated March 31, 2025 on its Grota do Cirilo project in Brazil's Lithium Valley describes pegmatites that average 12 m to 13 m thick at Xuxa and are 30 m to 35 m thick at Barreiro, and Pedrosa-Soares et al. (2025, Economic Geology, v. 120, no. 5) describe the pegmatites mined at Cachoeira since 1992 as decimeters to 30 m thick. This information is from the public sources cited and has not been verified by the Company or its Qualified Person. Outcrop widths and downhole intervals are not true thicknesses and are not on the same basis as the thicknesses reported in Brazil, and the comparison is of pegmatite thickness only, not of strike length, grade, tonnage, or mineralogy. The Springbok Project has no mineral resource estimate, and mineralization in Brazil is not necessarily indicative of mineralization at Springbok.



Figure 2: Brazil's Lithium Valley (Minas Gerais) and South Africa's Springbok District (Northern Cape) at the same map scale, showing license areas, mapped spodumene occurrences, and selected pegmatites. Thicknesses shown for Brazil are from Sigma Lithium Corporation's technical report dated March 31, 2025, and Pedrosa-Soares et al. (2025); Springbok outcrop widths are from the Company's technical report dated July 21, 2026, and are not true thicknesses. Information on Brazil is from public sources, has not been verified by the Company or its Qualified Person, and is not necessarily indicative of mineralization at Springbok, which has no mineral resource estimate.

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:
https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/11554/324825_d935e21414d28b19_002full.jpg

Drilling Continues Across the Springbok District

Drilling is continuing across the Springbok District to further define the potential of the Springbok Project. In 2026 the Company has drilled 138 holes across 14 pegmatite targets for approximately 4,330 m, including three follow-up holes (189 m) at Jackal Water and holes at Blesberg I (five holes, 105 m), Uranoop (seven holes, 182 m), Frankie (seven holes, 161 m), Kokerboomrand (eight holes, 280 m), and Spodumene Kop (16 holes, approximately 520 m) (Figure 2). Assays are pending, and results will be reported as they are received and validated.

At Norrabees I, diamond hole NB1DD26-006, collared inside the Company's five-hectare mining permit, returned 9.05 m at 1.19% Li2O from 1.95 m downhole, including 6.0 m at 1.44% Li2O from 4.0 m. Results from all 10 holes received from Norrabees I, V, and VIII, including holes with no significant intercepts, are in Table 1 (Appendix). Intervals are downhole lengths, and true widths are not yet known.

Sampling, Analysis, QA/QC and Data Verification

RC drilling was completed by Van Zyl Drilling using a face-sampling hammer. RC samples were collected over 1 m intervals through a riffle splitter, and a representative chip sample from each interval was retained in chip trays for logging. Diamond core from NB1DD26-005 and NB1DD26-006 was logged and sampled at nominal 1 m intervals adjusted to lithological contacts, and half-core was submitted for analysis. Sampling covered the logged pegmatite and 1 m to 2 m of adjacent host rock on either side of each pegmatite interval. Samples of approximately 2 kg were bagged, ticketed and sent to SGS South Africa (Randfontein) ("SGS"), an independent commercial laboratory accredited by SANAS to ISO/IEC 17025. Lithium was analyzed by sodium peroxide fusion with an ICP-AES finish (GE_ICP90A50) and a multi-element suite including cesium, rubidium and tantalum by sodium peroxide fusion with an ICP-MS finish (GE_IMS90A50).

The Company inserted a certified reference material every 20 samples, a blank every 50 samples, and a field duplicate every 10 samples. All certified reference material lithium results were within three standard deviations of the certified values, and all blanks returned lithium below or at the 10 ppm detection limit. Field duplicates showed acceptable repeatability, other than two core duplicate pairs from the spodumene-bearing interval in NB1DD26-006 and pairs below 200 ppm Li, where relative differences are large close to the detection limit. SGS's internal standards, blanks and repeats were also reviewed. Collar locations were recorded by handheld GPS.

The Qualified Person, Benjamin Gelber, P.Geo., has verified the assay database against the original laboratory certificates and considers the QA/QC results acceptable for the purpose of this release.

Qualified Person

The technical and scientific information in this news release was reviewed, verified and approved by Benjamin Gelber, P.Geo., a consultant of the Company and a practicing Professional Geologist registered with Engineers & Geoscientists British Columbia (EGBC, Licence No. 33258), who is a non-independent "Qualified Person" as defined by National Instrument 43-101 - Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects. The information on Brazil in this news release is taken from the public sources cited and has not been verified by the Qualified Person, and drill collar locations were recorded by handheld GPS. No other limitations on, or failures of, verification were identified.

About Lithium Africa Corp.

Lithium Africa Corp. is a lithium exploration and development company building a portfolio of hard-rock lithium assets across Africa. The Company holds the Springbok Project in South Africa directly and its exploration interests in West and Southern Africa, including the Adzopé District in Côte d'Ivoire, through a 50/50 joint venture with GFL International Co., Ltd., an affiliate of Ganfeng Lithium. For more information, please visit www.li-africa.com.

  • The Gleeson Project is Located on Private Land 28 Miles North of the Famous and Historic Bisbee Mining District
  • Intercepts Include 123.6 Meters Grading 0.91% Copper, 0.44 g/t Gold, and 5.27 g/t Silver from 601.70 Meters
  • Drilling Occurring on a Small Portion of Ivanhoe Electric's Land Package Consisting of Approximately 20,000 Acres of Mineral Rights and over 2,000 Acres of Private Surface Rights
  • Two Drill Rigs are Active with Further Assays to be Received in Coming Weeks

Phoenix, Arizona--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Ivanhoe Electric Inc. (NYSE American: IE) (TSX: IE) ("Ivanhoe Electric") Executive Chairman Robert Friedland and President and Chief Executive Officer Taylor Melvin are pleased to report the discovery of copper-gold-silver mineralization in the first drill holes on private land at the Company's Gleeson Copper-Gold Project ("Gleeson"). Gleeson is located in the historical Courtland-Gleeson Mining District in southeastern Arizona, 28 miles north of the world-famous historical Bisbee Mining District.

Mines in the Bisbee Mining District produced from 1880 to 2013 exploiting breccia, carbonate and intrusive-hosted deposits similar to mineralization styles at Gleeson.

Results from the first eleven completed drill holes have discovered two separate, significant mineralized domains at Gleeson below low angle faulting. Copper-gold-silver breccia has been logged in drill holes spanning an area of approximately 500 by 500 meters, from 600 meters depth, pinching out in the east to over 380 meters downhole thickness in the south-west. The breccia remains open in multiple directions. Below 1,000 meters depth, intrusive and carbonate replacement hosted copper-gold-silver-zinc mineralization has been discovered with mineralization logged in drillholes over 800 meters of north to south extent, 600 meters east to west and a strong vector to the west.

Ivanhoe Electric's Senior Vice President of Exploration, Alex Neufeld, commented: "The initial drill holes at Gleeson are the most impressive I have seen in my 20-year career at an early-stage exploration project. We are excited to announce that we have discovered two significant mineralized domains, with high-grade breccias and carbonate replacement mineralization. This is just the start of our search in this underappreciated, historic mining district which at this early stage is showing evidence that it may be analogous to the mineralization that underpinned the more than century of historic mining at Bisbee."

Highlights from the first holes include a significant interval in drill hole CGD26-TR-003, which also contained very high-grade copper-gold mineralization over shorter intervals (Photo 1)

  • Hole CGD26-TR-003: 123.60 meters at 0.91% copper, 0.44 g/t of gold and 5.27 g/t of silver from 601.70 meters, including:
    • 71.03 meters at 1.38% copper, 0.52 g/t of gold and 6.73 g/t of silver from 640.32 meters.



Photo 1: High-grade gold, copper and iron-sulfide mineralization in sample TR-003.0437 from the upper breccia domain grading 6.92% copper, 8.88 g/t of gold and 17.25 g/t of silver over 1.13 meters from 674.07 meters in hole CGD26-TR-003.

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:
https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/3868/324750_8599ff2664613a98_002full.jpg

Assay results from the first nine of eleven completed drill holes also include longer mineralized intervals at similar shallow depths within the breccia and contain shorter sub-intervals at higher grades. The breccia interval in CGD26-TR-008, around 250 meters southwest of CGD26-TR-003 returned:

  • Hole CGD26-TR-008: 381.66 meters at 0.34% copper, 0.29 g/t of gold and 1.07 g/t of silver from 587.85 meters, including:
    • 16.20 meters at 1.04% copper, 0.27 g/t of gold and 1.38 g/t of silver from 729.00 meters; and
    • 41.51 meters at 0.38% copper, 1.23 g/t of gold and 1.78 g/t of silver from 928.00 meters

The primary focus of Ivanhoe Electric's exploration efforts at Gleeson is on delineating the potential continuity and extensions of these mineralized domains. Initial drilling suggests an orientation to the southwest with the mineralization open in several directions. The possibility exists for several mineralized centers at Gleeson.

Mr. Friedland and Mr. Melvin commented: "Our Gleeson Copper-Gold Project in Arizona has suddenly become the Company's highest priority exploration project. These initial drill results are some of the best copper-gold-silver intercepts drilled in the Western United States in the last ten years. These initial discovery results provide us with a glimpse into what we think could become a major new copper-gold-silver district less than 30 miles north of the historic Bisbee District, one of America's most famous and prolific mining districts. Miners at Bisbee extracted over 200 million tonnes of ore from breccia, carbonate and intrusive-hosted mineralization over a 133-year period. Ivanhoe Electric controls a district scale land package that will allow us to explore the full potential of this significant new discovery in this emerging new district, with Gleeson being the focus of what we believe is the best copper-gold-silver exploration project in the United States."

Additional drilling shows visible sulfide mineralization in both breccia and carbonate-replacement domains, with assays expected in the coming weeks

Holes CGD26-TR-008 and CGD26-TR-009 have intersected zones of carbonate replacement mineralization from depths of approximately 1,250 meters (Photos 2, 3 and 4). Assays are in progress with results expected before the end of 2026.

The Gleeson Copper-Gold Project is an emerging copper-gold district north of the historic Bisbee Mining District covering approximately 20,000 acres of mineral rights and 2,000 acres of private surface rights held by Ivanhoe Electric

The Gleeson Copper-Gold Project is located within the historic Courtland-Gleeson Mining District, approximately 28 miles north of Bisbee (Figure 1).

Ivanhoe Electric started acquiring mineral and surface rights in 2024, and currently controls over 19,606 acres of mineral rights and 2,033 acres of private surface rights. The world-famous Bisbee Mining District to the south of Gleeson produced almost continuously from 1880 to 2013, exploiting porphyry and breccia-hosted mineralization intruded into limestones with carbonate-replacement and skarn-type deposits. Over its 133-year life, over 207 million tonnes of ore was mined yielding approximately 8.2 billion pounds of copper, 2.8 million ounces of gold, 105 million ounces of silver, 145,000 tonnes of lead, and 161,000 tonnes of zinc, making it Arizona's largest gold producer, top lead producer, and second-largest silver producer.

Technical Information and Qualified Person

Disclosures of a scientific or technical nature in this news release have been reviewed and approved by Shawn Vandekerkhove, P.Geo., Vice President, Partnerships and New Opportunities of Ivanhoe Electric. Mr. Vandekerkhove is a "qualified person" as defined in Subpart 1300 of Regulation S-K and a "qualified person" as defined in National Instrument 43-101 Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects. Mr. Vandekerkhove is an employee of Ivanhoe Electric and is not independent of the Company within the meaning of NI 43-101.

Mr. Vandekerkhove verified the sampling and analytical data supporting the reported results. During site visits, he observed drilling, logging, core cutting, sampling and shipment, checked selected collars and drill setups, and examined core from the principal mineralized zones. He checked several dozen randomly selected assays against original laboratory certificates from multiple batches, independently recalculated the reported composites, reviewed their endpoints and reviewed the program's QA/QC results. His review identified no recovery or QA/QC issues that could materially affect the reliability of the reported results. There were no limitations on the verification.

Ivanhoe Electric employs industry best-practice QA/QC and data verification protocols. The diamond drill holes were completed using PQ, HQ, and NQ diameters. The drill core was cut lengthwise into halves using a diamond-bladed saw, with one-half used for the assay sample and the other half retained in core boxes and archived on site. Pulps and rejects are also stored on site for archival purposes. Mineralized zones were generally sampled on 2-meter intervals. Samples were broken at lithological, mineralization, and alteration domain breaks. Each core sample was placed into a bag with a unique numbered sample identification tag. Quality control samples including blanks, duplicates, and certified reference materials were inserted between core samples in a predefined sequence. Then samples were grouped into batches for shipping and laboratory submissions. Chain of custody records are maintained for sample shipments, and the custody is transferred from Ivanhoe Electric to the laboratory preparation facility upon delivery.

Samples were shipped to ALS Laboratories in Tucson, Arizona, for sample preparation and subsequently analyzed at ALS Laboratories in North Vancouver, British Columbia. Samples were analyzed using customary four acid digestion and ICP-MS finish (ME-MS61). A standard gold fire assay package was used to analyze for gold (Au-ICP21). ME-OG62 was used to analyze for overlimit Cu, Ag, Pb, and Zn; some Ag were further analyzed using gravimetric finish (Ag-GRA21) depending on silver concentrations. ALS Laboratories in North Vancouver, British Columbia, is an independent laboratory accredited to ISO/IEC 17025:2017 by the Standards Council of Canada for the analytical methods performed.

Qualification milestones expand device options for mission-critical space applications

CHANDLER, Ariz., Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Microchip Technology (Nasdaq: MCHP) is strengthening its portfolio of high-reliability aerospace and defense solutions with new spaceflight qualifications for its radiation-tolerant (RT) PolarFire® FPGA and SoC families. The RT PolarFire FPGA RTPF500ZT has achieved Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Qualified Manufacturers List (QML) Class V qualification, the highest qualification standard for space microelectronics. Additionally, the RT PolarFire SoC FPGA RTPFS460ZT has completed QML Class Q and MIL-STD-883 Class B qualifications. These milestones provide developers with flight-ready components for systems with stringent reliability requirements.

“As space applications demand greater onboard processing capability within increasingly constrained SWaP budgets, developers need technologies that maximize performance without increasing power consumption or thermal complexity,” said Shakeel Peera, corporate vice president of Microchip’s FPGA business unit. “Our RT PolarFire portfolio combines a power-efficient, radiation-tolerant architecture designed to be immune to radiation-induced upsets and defense-grade security to help developers reduce system power, simplify thermal management and build highly integrated, mission-critical space systems.”

 The majority of SRAM-based FPGAs typically require configuration scrubbing to correct radiation-induced upsets which can remain undetected between scrubbing cycles and increase power consumption. RT PolarFire devices use configuration technology designed to eliminate configuration Single-Event Upset (SEU) concerns. The devices’ power-efficient operation helps address the thermal limits of space platforms, and defense-grade security helps protect mission-critical systems while reducing system complexity. With high reliability and radiation tolerance, RT PolarFire devices are designed for aerospace and defense applications, from satellite payloads and constellations to human-rated spacecraft and deep-space missions.

The flight proven QML-V qualified RTPF500ZT PolarFire FPGA features Single-Event Latch-Up (SEL) radiation performance and in-flight programmability for mission-critical space applications requiring high reliability for demanding missions. The RTPFS460ZT PolarFire SoC FPGA combines programmable logic with an integrated Microprocessor Subsystem (MSS) featuring 64-bit RISC-V® processor cores and is qualified to MIL-STD-883 Class B and QML Class Q. Available development kits, together with a common RT PolarFire architecture and tool flow help streamline evaluation, prototyping and flight-system development.

MIL-STD-883 and QML qualification establish testing, manufacturing and quality requirements for microelectronic devices used in high-reliability aerospace and defense applications. MIL-STD-883 defines uniform environmental, mechanical and electrical test methods, while QML Class V under MIL-PRF-38535 establishes space-level quality and reliability assurance requirements. Together, these requirements help customers address stringent reliability and mission assurance needs for critical space applications. Visit the website to learn more about Microchip’s full portfolio of radiation-tolerant FPGAs.

Development Tools
The RTPFS460ZT development kit enables evaluation and prototyping of the RT PolarFire SoC FPGA, and both devices are supported by Microchip’s Libero® SoC Design Suite for overall design and development and the Mi-V® ecosystem for RISC-V development. Together, these resources provide a cohesive environment to evaluate the architecture, validate designs and reuse engineering work as programs progress toward flight hardware.

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Spartan Metals Corp. (TSXV: W) (OTCQB: SPRMF) (FSE: J03) ("Spartan" or the "Company") is pleased to announce the positive results of a Preliminary Economic Assessment ("PEA") for its Victorio Tungsten-Molybdenum Project ("Victorio" or the "Project") in Luna County, New Mexico. SRK Consulting ("SRK") led preparation of the PEA, with Teal CPG, Inc. ("Teal") contributing the previously announced mineral resource estimate (see news release October 22, 2026). The PEA has an effective date of September 21, 2026. All monetary amounts are in U.S. dollars unless otherwise stated. A technical report prepared in accordance with National Instrument 43-101 Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects ("NI 43-101") will be filed on SEDAR+ (www.sedarplus.ca) and on the Company's website within 45 days of this news release.

Brett Marsh, Spartan's President and CEO comments, "We are thrilled about the opportunity this PEA outlines for the Victorio Project. Using realistic, long-term metals prices of US$1,350/mtu WO₃ and US$20/lb molybdenum, the study estimates an after-tax NPV8 of US$2.14 billion and a 30.9% IRR. Both metals contribute to those economics, so continued price appreciation for either metal can make a meaningful difference to the underlying project economics."

Mr. Marsh continues, "We're looking at a potential 24-year operation, with modelled cumulative, undiscounted after-tax free cash flow of US$6.9 billion before financing costs, with an estimated 3.2-year after-tax payback of the initial capital investment of US$683.0 million. Higher metal price scenarios highlights Victorio's substantial potential upside to metal prices. At US$2,000/mtu WO₃ and US$25/lb molybdenum, which are still below current market prices; the after-tax NPV8 rises to nearly twice the base case NPV at US$4.02 billion and the IRR reaches 43.3%. Our team has also identified potential by-product opportunities with fluorspar and beryllium, which may contribute meaningful upside to the project economics and will be addressed in future studies."

Mr. Marsh concludes, "Having this opportunity in New Mexico is significant as it's a solid mining jurisdiction with excellent infrastructure in the vicinity of the Project. Victorio, which is supported by the results of this PEA, could become a lasting domestic source of tungsten and molybdenum for U.S. industrial and defense customers. This is a major milestone for Spartan, and we're eager to advance the technical work, permitting, financing and product qualification required to move the Victorio project forward."

Next Steps and Development Considerations

Advancing Victorio toward a development decision will require further resource evaluation, mine design, metallurgical testing, engineering, environmental studies and permitting, together with financing. Areas requiring further assessment include underground ground conditions, water supply, tailings design, product quality and commercial terms, and the timing and cost of sustaining development.

Mineral Resource Basis

The Victorio Mineral Resource estimate was prepared by Teal CPG, Inc. and has an effective date of August 3, 2026. Conceptual Operating Plan

The PEA evaluates an underground block cave operation feeding a molybdenum flotation circuit and an ammonium paratungstate ("APT") plant. The conceptual schedule processes approximately 199.5 million U.S. short tons over 24 operating years. Block cave mining is an underground mining method that uses gravity to help break and move large masses of rock. Tunnels are built beneath the deposit, and a supporting layer is removed to allow the rock above to break and fall to collection points. Block cave can produce large volumes of ore at relatively low operating costs, although substantial underground development is required before production begins.

An APT plant uses chemical treatments to dissolve the tungsten from concentrate, remove any potential impurities and form crystals ready for sale to end consumers. Manufacturers convert APT into tungsten metal and tungsten carbide, used in cutting tools, industrial equipment and other specialized products. Producing APT on site would place Victorio's output at a key intermediate stage of the tungsten supply chain.

Metal Prices and Long-term Supply Opportunity

The PEA base case uses US$1,350/mtu WO₃ as a long-term planning price, supported by a long-term market assessment commissioned by Spartan from Fastmarkets1 and accepted by the qualified person responsible for the economic analysis. The base case retains US$20/lb Mo. The US$2,000/mtu WO₃ and US$25/lb Mo sensitivity moves closer to the dated spot market references below, while remaining below both benchmarks.

The base case tungsten price is approximately 49% below the cited market indications and is supported by Fastmarkets' long-term assessment1, while the higher-case tungsten price is approximately 25% below the cited market indications. The US$20/lb Mo is approximately 42% below the cited LME market indication and the US$25/lb Mo is approximately 27% below the LME futures. Regional prices and product terms differ, and actual prices will vary over the Project's life.

S&P Global's October 2026 report expects tungsten demand to grow approximately 10% between 2026 and 2030 and estimates that China supplies about 80% of mine production and 85% of APT. Industrial uses, defense and technology applications support demand, while export restrictions and the time needed to finance, permit and commission new mines and processing plants can slow supply growth. This disconnect between expected demand and the pace of qualified supply is a consideration in the long-term price assumptions. Announced projects and restarts can add capacity, with delivery timing remaining important.

Molybdenum supply comes from primary mines and as a byproduct of copper mining, tying part of its growth to copper operations and investment. Recent European tightness and expectations of constrained mine output have supported prices. These conditions provide upside exposure, while steel demand and new production can change the balance.

Major discoveries cannot be assumed to provide timely new supply: resource definition, engineering, permitting, construction and product qualification can take many years. The limited pool of advanced domestic tungsten supply options makes the development pipeline particularly relevant to U.S. defense sourcing. From January 1, 2027, DFARS 252.225-7052 extends covered-country restrictions for specified tungsten products back through the ore and feedstock stages, subject to its exceptions, which can impact U.S. demand.

Victorio's New Mexico location and 24-year operating concept position it as a potential long-term domestic source of tungsten and an additional source of molybdenum alongside existing U.S. production. This could support industrial and defense supply diversification if the Project is advanced successfully. Development remains subject to further technical studies, permitting and financing. Supplying defense customers would also require appropriate product quality, traceability and downstream qualifications.

Property Exploration Summary and Highlights:

The Perestroika Prospect lies along a structural corridor of intense deformation and alteration within the WNW-ESE trending Uniacke Deformation Corridor, inferred as the southeastern strike extension of the prolific Destor-Porcupine Deformation Zone. Previous exploration work located on the Perestroika Prospect established the presence of a gold mineralized trend hosting two (2) historical surface showings, referred to as the "Uniacke Shear" and "Glasnost" gold occurrences. In 2009, drilling by Golden Valley Mines and Royalties Ltd. successfully intersected multiple zones of high-grade gold mineralization associated with these historical gold showings, including drill intersections of 1.15 metres averaging 59.52 g/t Au, including 0.30 metres grading 217 g/t Au in GPS09-01 and 3.50 metres averaging 18.08 g/t Au, including 3.05 metres averaging 20.69 g/t Au in GPS09-02 (GM 54860).

This Phase III diamond drilling program intended to follow-up on promising gold values from the 2009 Golden Valley Mines and Royalties Ltd. drill program results and the subsequent Eldorado operated drill programs in 2024 and 2025. Final assays from 2026 RC Program Continue to Expand Deposit's Dimensions

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - North Arrow Minerals Inc. (TSXV: NAR) (OTCQB: NHAWF) (FSE: 9TB) ("North Arrow" or the "Company") today reports results from the final seven of sixteen reverse circulation ("RC") holes completed during Rotation 4 at the Kraaipan Gold Project ("Kraaipan") in southern Botswana. Five holes were drilled at Tlou (Target AE): one infill hole and one step-out to the north, one deeper hole testing the down-dip extent of mineralization, and two scissor holes to help define its geometry. All five intersected gold mineralization with four intersecting broad zones of mineralization comparable to earlier 2026 results at Tlou. Two holes at Nkwe (Target AF) tested the southern extension of Grid 1 and intersected narrow zones of mineralization.

With these results, all 14 Rotation 4 holes at Tlou have intersected gold mineralization. North Arrow drilling has now traced the mineralized trend over approximately 750 metres of strike, from KR26-099 in the south to KR26-102 in the north, and historical drilling by previous operators intersected the same favourable contact a further 200 m to the south. Mineralization at Tlou remains open along strike and at depth.

Key Highlights

  • Consistent, broad mineralization along close to one kilometre of strike - Rotation 4 drilling has returned wide zones of gold mineralization from surface along the Tlou trend, including 1.17 g/t Au over 42 m in KR26-095 (reported November 4, 2026) and 0.63 g/t Au over 48 m in KR26-108 (reported today).
  • KR26-108 infill hole returns 0.63 g/t Au over 48 m from 20 m depth, including 0.91 g/t Au over 23 m. KR26-108 was drilled between KR26-043 (0.57 g/t Au over 35 m) and KR26-100 (0.36 g/t Au over 45 m).
  • Deepest hole at Tlou ends in mineralization - KR26-105 returned 0.57 g/t Au over 15 m from 121 m down hole, including 1.68 g/t Au over the final 2 m, extending mineralization to more than 100 m vertical depth. Quartz veining with fresh pyrite was logged at the end of the hole.
  • Scissor holes support a steep to sub-vertical geometry - KR26-107 returned 0.64 g/t Au over 26 m, including 0.96 g/t Au over 14 m, and KR26-106 returned 0.48 g/t Au over 27 m, including 0.96 g/t Au over 7 m.
  • Gold is not restricted to banded iron formation - much of the higher-grade interval in KR26-108 lies within a unit logged as altered possible mafic rock interbedded with approximately equal proportions of ferruginous chert. Together with earlier results in altered mafic rocks and hematite-altered iron-rich rocks, this enhances the understanding of gold mineralization associations with the KGB and will assist in effective targeting.

CEO Commentary

Eira Thomas, Chief Executive Officer of North Arrow, stated:

"Tlou continues to develop into a coherent discovery. Every hole we have drilled on this trend in Rotation 4 has intersected zones of gold mineralization, and our drilling now traces those zones over approximately 750 metres, within a trend of close to one kilometre that remains open along strike and at depth. Our deepest hole ended in mineralization, and we are seeing gold in what are possibly mafic rocks as well as in banded iron formation, which deepens our understanding of gold mineralization associations within the Kraaipan Greenstone Belt. Broad zones of gold associated with BIF, quartz veining and pyrite are characteristic of Harmony's Kalgold mine, 40 kilometres to the south, and that is the model we are now testing. We finish 2026 with three discoveries - Tlou, Nkwe and Tau - and a clear set of targets for core drilling in 2027."

Drilling Summary

Sixteen RC drill holes, totalling 1,075 m were completed during Rotation 4: 14 at Tlou (968 m) and two at Nkwe (107 m). Results for the first nine holes, all at Tlou, were reported on November 4, 2026. Table 1 summarizes all 16 holes, Figure 1 shows the locations of the three discoveries, Figure 2 shows hole locations at Tlou and Table 2 summarizes assay results for the seven holes reported today.

Tlou RC Drilling Results

Five holes reported today complete the 14-hole Tlou program. The program was designed to test the northern and southern strike extent of the mineralization first drilled in May 2026 (see news release dated July 15, 2026), to test its down-dip extent and to help resolve its geometry (Figures 2 and 3).

Figure 2: Tlou Rotation 4 RC drill holes, select results

Tlou North

KR26-108 was drilled as an infill hole between KR26-043 (0.57 g/t Au over 35 m, including 1.72 g/t Au over 7 m) and KR26-100 (0.36 g/t Au over 45 m). It returned 0.63 g/t Au over 48 m from 20 m down hole, including 0.91 g/t Au over 23 m, consistent with the wide intervals in neighbouring holes. Much of the 23-metre interval lies within a unit logged altered possible mafic rock interbedded with approximately equal proportions of ferruginous chert.

KR26-102 was collared 60 m north of KR26-101 and returned 0.31 g/t Au over 10 m, including 0.51 g/t Au over 2 m. The hole confirms that the mineralized system continues northward. The footwall rock package becomes more varied to the north, and the sand cover in this area means the full package may not yet have been tested.

Tlou Main: down-dip and scissor holes

KR26-105 was drilled from the east to test mineralization below KR26-039 and KR26-040 (1.11 g/t Au over 27 m). It returned 0.57 g/t Au over 15 m from 121 m down hole, including 1.68 g/t Au over the final 2 m, and ended in mineralization at 136 m. The interval lies approximately 105-118 m below surface, the deepest mineralization intersected at Tlou to date. The lower part of the hole intersected chert-rich BIF with dense quartz veining, chlorite alteration and disseminated pyrite. Mineralization remains open at depth.

KR26-106 and KR26-107 were drilled from the west as scissor holes. Both passed through variably altered and sheared mafic rocks before intersecting altered ferruginous chert and BIF. KR26-107 returned 0.64 g/t Au over 26 m, including 0.96 g/t Au over 14 m, and KR26-106 returned 0.48 g/t Au over 27 m, including 0.96 g/t Au over 7 m. Together with KR26-105, these holes indicate that the mineralized zone is steep to sub-vertical, or dips steeply west, at this location (Figure 3). Logging suggests locally thickening of the alteration and veining, and further work is needed to define these controls.

Gold in Multiple Host Rocks

BIF and ferruginous chert remain the primary exploration target at Kraaipan, as they are at Kalgold. Drilling at Tlou now shows that gold also occurs in other rock types:

  • Mafic rocks: much of the 0.91 g/t Au over 23 m interval in KR26-108 lies within a unit comprising a mixture of altered possible mafic rock and ferruginous chert. KR26-095 returned 0.84 g/t Au over 4 m from an altered, quartz-veined mafic unit (November 4, 2026).
  • Iron-rich, hematite-altered rocks: KR26-100 returned 0.56 g/t Au over 16 m from a massive, hematite-altered, variably magnetic unit with no discernible quartz veining.
  • Quartz veins: outcropping northwest-trending quartz veins with shallow to moderate northeast dips cut the north-trending stratigraphy. Gold is associated with these veins and their altered selvages in drill holes, and in surface samples at Tlou, Nkwe and Tau (Aug 24 2026, July 15 2026, April 16 2026, Feb 27,2026).

Fresh pyrite in KR26-105 confirms the association of sulphides with altered vein selvages and with silicified, iron-flooded ferruginous chert and BIF. The presence of quartz veining, sulphides and potentially replacement-style alteration in other altered rocks (possibly mafics) expands the potential host units for mineralization beyond BIF and ferruginous chert. These observations assist in better understanding the gold associations and will inform future targeting. The relationship between mineralization in non-BIF units and the regional structure will be a focus of mapping and geochemical interpretation.

Nkwe RC Drilling

Two holes were drilled south of Grid 1 at Nkwe to test the strike extent of mineralization intersected in KR26-021 (4.04 g/t Au over 9 m; see news release dated July 15, 2026). KR26-104 returned 0.96 g/t Au over 2 m and KR26-103 returned 0.44 g/t Au over 1 m, both in narrow zones of altered, quartz-veined ferruginous chert and foliated mafic rock, extending near-surface mineralization at Nkwe to more than [550] metres of strike.

As previously reported, the 2026 exploration budget was increased from US$2.3 million to US$2.86 million to accommodate Rotation 4 drilling, expanded rock sampling and new soil sampling grids.

Next Steps

  • Interpretation of Tlou results and planning of a 2027 core drilling program to test the geometry, continuity and depth extent of mineralization.
  • Integration of RC results into regional targeting, incorporating the improved understanding of the gold associations generated from 2026 results.
  • Hyperspectral scanning of representative 2025 and 2026 RC chips was completed in early Q4 2026; results are being compiled.
  • Surface prospecting, soil sampling and ground geophysics will continue across the property.

About the Kraaipan Gold Project

The Kraaipan Project comprises approximately 724 km² of mineral concessions covering the entire ~60 km northern extension of the Kraaipan Greenstone Belt, a highly prospective Archean greenstone terrain straddling the Botswana-South Africa border. Over 80% of the northern portion of the belt is covered by Kalahari overburden, which has seen limited past exploration. The South African portion of the belt hosts numerous mineral occurrences including Harmony Gold's Kalgold Mine, a multi-million-ounce, BIF-hosted gold operation located 40 km to the south that has been in continuous production for over 30 years. Mineralization at Kalgold is not necessarily indicative of mineralization on the Kraaipan Project.

North Arrow can earn up to 80% interest in the Kraaipan Project from Rockman Resources through a First Option to earn 60% by investing US$5 M over three years (US$1 M firm commitment achieved), and a Second Option, at Rockman's election, to earn an additional 20% upon completion of a Preliminary Economic Assessment. North Arrow's partner Rockman Resources - through its operator Mineral Services - leverages over 25 years of operational experience in Botswana, together with proprietary technologies including high-resolution UAV magnetics, a mobile RC drilling platform optimized for Kalahari conditions, and in-house sample preparation.

Sampling, Laboratory Analyses and QA/QC

RC and surface rock samples collected in the field were driven to Mineral Services' facility in Gaborone to be sorted and prioritized for assay. Samples were allocated unique random sample numbers, sealed and shipped to ALS's laboratory in Johannesburg, South Africa using industry-standard chain-of-custody protocols. Following an initial coarse crush (CRU-21), the entire sample is then pulverized (PUL-21) to better than 85% passing a 75-micron screen prior to geochemical analysis. All samples are analyzed for gold by fire assay with an ICP-AES finish, method code Au-ICP22 (50-gram sample). Samples returning gold values over 10 ppm are subjected to ore-grade check assays using fire assay and a gravimetric finish using method code Au-GRA22 (50-gram sample). Samples are also subjected to lithium borate fusion and acid digestion for whole-rock analysis of major and trace elements by ICP-AES (major elements) and ICP-MS (trace elements); method codes ME-ICP06 and ME-MS81, respectively. In addition, a suite of base metals and other trace elements not included in the ME-MS81 method are analysed by ICP-AES on four-acid digestions (method code ME-4ACD81).

QA/QC protocols include ALS laboratory's own internal quality assurance controls as well as Rockman's field controls, including the insertion of duplicates and certified reference materials (CRM), each at a rate of roughly one per 20 samples. QA/QC data are evaluated on receipt for failures, and appropriate action is taken if results for duplicates, CRMs and blanks fall outside allowed tolerances.

North Arrow Minerals is a Vancouver-based exploration company focused on evaluating the Kraaipan Gold Project. Management and advisors bring significant global exploration and mining experience. PRINCETON, N.J.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Bristol Myers Squibb (NYSE: BMY) today announced it will present new data from its robust hematology portfolio through more than 90 company- and partner-sponsored disclosures, including 24 oral presentations, at the 68th American Society of Hematology (ASH) Annual Meeting and Exposition, taking place in New Orleans, Louisiana, from December 12-15, 2026.

“This has been an extraordinary year across our blood cancer portfolio, and what we’re sharing at ASH is the realization of our scientific investments,” said Cristian Massacesi, MD, executive vice president, chief medical officer and head of development, Bristol Myers Squibb. “At ASH, we’re highlighting the breadth of our work in blood cancers from Phase 3 CELMoD datasets in multiple myeloma, exploration of targeted protein degradation’s potential in follicular lymphoma, five-year landmark survival data for Breyanzi and the clinical potential of our dual-targeted CAR T, tunlucabtagene autoleucel. Together, these advancements reflect one goal: to move beyond the current standard management of blood cancers and redefine what patients can expect from treatment.”

Data presented by Bristol Myers Squibb will underscore both the strength of the Company’s commercial portfolio and the rapid momentum of its innovative early- and late-stage pipeline in targeted protein degradation, including CELMoDs and other protein degradation approaches, alongside next-generation autologous CAR T cell therapy.

Key data being presented at ASH by Bristol Myers Squibb and its collaborators include:

Evolving multiple myeloma through powerful CELMoD combinations and next-generation cell therapies

  • Phase 3 EXCALIBER-RRMM progression-free survival (PFS) and minimal residual disease results for ZENBEXUS, daratumumab, and dexamethasone versus daratumumab, bortezomib and dexamethasone in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM), to be featured in oral presentation
  • Phase 1 safety and efficacy results for dual-targeting BCMA×GPRC5D autologous CAR T cell therapy tunlucabtagene autoleucel (tunlu-cel; BMS-986453) in patients with RRMM, to be featured in oral presentation
  • PFS results and outcomes by prior exposure to pomalidomide or T-cell-redirecting therapy from the SUCCESSOR-2 study evaluating mezigdomide, carfilzomib, and dexamethasone versus carfilzomib and dexamethasone (Kd) in patients with RRMM
  • Phase 1 arlocabtagene autoleucel (arlo-cel) oral presentation on GPRC5D expression and locus integrity in patients with RRMM
  • Initial Phase 1 results evaluating mezigdomide in combination with elranatamab for the treatment of RRMM

Advancing lymphoma care with targeted protein degradation and curative intent

  • Phase 2 GOLSEEK-2 results for golcadomide, an investigational oral CELMoD agent, plus rituximab in patients with newly-diagnosed advanced-stage follicular lymphoma, to be featured in oral presentation
  • Landmark five-year follow-up from the pivotal Phase 3 TRANSFORM study demonstrating the curative potential of Breyanzi in second-line (2L) relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL)
  • Evaluation of real-world effectiveness and safety outcomes for Breyanzi versus bispecific antibodies in 2L LBCL

Delivering disease breadth and leadership in myeloid disorders

  • Phase 2 results for Reblozyl® (luspatercept-aamt) in adults with non-transfusion-dependent (NTD) α-thalassemia hemoglobin H (HbH) disease, to be featured in oral presentation
  • Phase 2a results for Reblozyl in adolescents with transfusion-dependent (TD) β-thalassemia, to be featured in oral presentation
